subject.title: feat(plugins): add exact-profile provider usage reads

question: Should `api.runtime.providerUsage.read` be a public capability for third-party plugins, and if so which trusted-install or explicit capability boundary must authorize provider-auth-backed profile reads?
rationale: The PR documents a trusted-plugin use case but the runtime bridge currently gates only on agent scope; selecting the permanent caller and permission contract is a maintainer security and API decision, not a mechanical follow-up.

options.title: Keep the seam internal for now
options.body: Do not publish the SDK method; let the approved user-facing usage implementation own exact-profile reads until a broader plugin contract is designed.

options.title: Publish a capability-gated API
options.body: Define the supported plugin class and enforce that authorization before profile resolution, then document and test both allowed and denied callers.

options.title: Accept unrestricted plugin access
options.body: Explicitly accept that any installed plugin with agent execution scope may request sanitized usage data for profile IDs it knows.

recommendation.title: Keep the seam internal for now
recommendation.body: Do not publish the SDK method; let the approved user-facing usage implementation own exact-profile reads until a broader plugin contract is designed.

likelyOwner.reason: They can provide the implementation and intended consumer context, while a plugin SDK/security maintainer still needs to make the approval decision.
